t: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the United States courthouse referred to in section 1 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “George E. Brown, Jr. United States Courthouse”.

fable.w: This is a boilerplate naming provision that redirects references in federal records to the courthouse's new name. The word "regulation" might tempt a rulemaking reading, but it appears only in a list of record types, not as a grant of rulemaking authority. No outside party is consulted, heard, or given any right in a federal decision.
fable.s: shall be deemed to be a reference to the “George E. Brown, Jr. United States Courthouse”

opus.w: This is a standard naming provision: it says that references to the courthouse in federal records should be read as references to the "George E. Brown, Jr. United States Courthouse." No one outside the federal government is consulted, and there is no hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue. The word "regulation" appears only in a list of records and does not authorize any rulemaking, so it does not count as participation.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a purely administrative directive regarding the naming convention for a federal building in official records. It does not involve any consultation, coordination, or interaction with parties outside the federal government. There is no advisory board, public comment period, or requirement to consult with states, tribes, or the public.
qwen_chat.s: Any reference in a law, map, regulation, document, paper, or other record of the United States to the United States courthouse referred to in section 1 shall be deemed to be a reference to the “George E. Brown, Jr. United States Courthouse”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that renaming a building involves public input or consultation, but the text itself contains no such requirement. It is purely a directive on how to interpret references in official records.
